claim.quote: we are able to deduce a value of about 120 MeV for the temperature at thermal freeze-out

name: NA44 particle production and freeze-out in central Pb+Pb collisions

summary.plain: NA44 measured pions, kaons and protons from central lead-lead collisions at 158 GeV per nucleon. The mass dependence of their momentum spectra implies a thermal freeze-out near 120 MeV, and particle ratios give a chemical freeze-out near 140 MeV.
summary.technical: Single-particle inclusive spectra of pi+-, K+-, p and anti-p versus transverse mass near mid-rapidity in central 158A GeV/c Pb+Pb: the mass dependence of the mT distributions gives about 120 MeV for the thermal freeze-out temperature; the rapidity-density ratios give light- and strange-quark chemical potentials and a chemical freeze-out temperature of approximately 140 MeV.

title: Particle production in central Pb+Pb collisions at 158 A GeV/c
why_it_matters: Part of NA44's measurement of collective (radial) flow and freeze-out, which the 2026 SPS review calls probably the most important NA44 contribution to the field.
